"""The word 'school' in any language, as it is spelled out.

The component fires on the token that completes a word meaning "school": 'school',
'schools', 'Schule', 'scuola', 'escuela', 'école', 'skola', 'школа', '学校', and the
like, plus the short ending of such a word (Schul+en, Escol+ar). It is strongest on a
bare 'School' naming an institution ('the School of ...', 'Icahn School'), and
it is weak when 'school' is a grade level ('high school', 'middle school'). Words
that merely contain the letters (scholar, scholarship, Schultz, Schuld) do not fire.
It predicts 0 everywhere else.
"""
import re

READS = ()

# spellings of "school" (matched inside a word, lowercase)
STEMS = ("school", "schul", "scuol", "scol", "escol", "escuel", "école", "ecole",
         "skol", "škol", "szko", "shkol", "школ", "σχολ", "学校", "スクール")
NOT_SCHOOL = ("scholar", "schuld", "schulter", "schultz", "schulz", "preschool")
GRADE_LEVELS = {"high", "middle"}                      # 'high school': barely fires
MODIFIERS = {"elementary", "primary", "secondary", "law", "graduate", "charter", "business"}


def is_school_word(word):
    return any(s in word for s in STEMS) and not any(s in word for s in NOT_SCHOOL)


def last_word(text):
    """The letters at the end of the text ('' if it ends in a non-letter)."""
    m = re.search(r"[^\W\d_]+\Z", text)
    return m.group(0).lower() if m else ""


def word_before_last(text):
    """The last whole word before the text's final word, ignoring spaces and punctuation."""
    text = re.sub(r"[^\W\d_]+\Z", "", text)
    m = re.search(r"([^\W\d_]+)\W*\Z", text)
    return m.group(1).lower() if m else ""


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip()
    same_doc = len(prefix.document_ids) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]
    cur = prefix.text_prefixes[-1][-80:]                      # text up to this token
    prev = prefix.text_prefixes[-2][-80:] if same_doc else ""  # text up to the last token
    word, last = last_word(cur), last_word(prev)

    # the token that completes a school word
    if is_school_word(word) and not is_school_word(last):
        before = word_before_last(cur)
        if before in GRADE_LEVELS:
            return carry, 0.5
        if before in MODIFIERS:
            return carry, 2.5
        return carry, 7.0 if token == "School" else 6.0

    # a short ending added to a school word: Schul+en, Escol+ar
    if is_school_word(word) and is_school_word(last) and word.startswith(last) \
            and len(word) - len(last) <= 3 and any(last.endswith(x) for x in STEMS):
        return carry, 5.0

    # 'of' right after a school name: 'School of ...'
    if token.lower() == "of" and is_school_word(last):
        if word_before_last(prev) not in GRADE_LEVELS | MODIFIERS:
            return carry, 7.0
    return carry, 0.0

"""Component layers.1.mlp.down_proj:5981: a "first token of a document" detector.

The model's attention is reset at every document boundary (and at the start of each packed
row), so the first token of a document has no context before it. At exactly that token this
component fires, strongly, and how strongly depends on what the token looks like:

- a capitalised word, especially a short one ("The", "I", "An")  ........ large (4 to 6.5)
- a lowercase word or word-piece .................................... medium (3 to 4)
- punctuation or a symbol, short ones low, long ones (e.g. "<|im_start|>") high
- a digit ........................................................... slightly negative
- a whitespace-only token ........................................... about zero

At every other position it is essentially silent (its activation stays within about +-0.2).

The values are the mean activations observed on training rows for each class of first token,
not a per-token fit. Token classes are read off the token's text alone.
"""

READS = ()

# Mean activation on a document's first token, keyed by
# (kind of first character, token has a leading space, token is at most 3 characters).
GAIN = {
    ("upper", False, False): 3.9,
    ("upper", False, True): 6.4,
    ("upper", True, False): 3.1,
    ("upper", True, True): 5.0,
    ("lower", False, False): 4.2,
    ("lower", False, True): 4.0,
    ("lower", True, False): 2.9,
    ("lower", True, True): 3.5,
    ("punct", False, False): 5.8,
    ("punct", False, True): 2.3,
    ("punct", True, False): 2.1,
    ("punct", True, True): 2.1,
    ("digit", False, True): -0.5,
}


def key(token):
    """(kind of the first visible character, leading space, short) for a token's text."""
    body = token.lstrip()
    if not body:
        return None
    first = body[0]
    if first.isdigit():
        kind = "digit"
    elif first.isalpha():
        kind = "upper" if first.isupper() else "lower"
    else:
        kind = "punct"
    return kind, token.startswith(" "), len(body) <= 3


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """The activation at the newest token: its class's mean if it starts a document, else 0."""
    starts_document = prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    if not starts_document:
        return carry, 0.0
    return carry, float(GAIN.get(key(prefix.token_strings[-1]), 0.0))

near zero on most tokens and jumps on a handful of recognisable patterns:

  1. The digit 3 that starts a number, followed by 0 or 1 (times and dates such as
     "3:30", "March 31"): strong (about 1.2 for "30", 0.7 for "31"). A 3 that is the
     last digit of a longer number ("13", "123") gives a weaker 0.4.
  2. A LaTeX line break, the two-character token backslash-backslash, inside maths

  3. The same backslash-backslash inside an escaped code string (it is followed by
     an escaped quote or n, as in printed code inside a JSON string): negative, -1.2.
  4. Indentation (2 to 8 spaces or tabs) that starts a line: 0.6 when the text
     before it is a line-numbered listing (lines like "  123<TAB>code"), 0.3 otherwise.
     Indentation in the middle of a line gives 0.

"""Single-letter word starts.

The component fires on a token that is a single letter standing alone as a word or
segment: after a space, a slash or a dot, or at the start of a line, and not inside a
longer word. Its size depends on the alphabet and the case: Greek, Arabic, Hebrew and
Cyrillic letters after a space are the strongest; Latin capitals are weaker than
lowercase letters; a letter continuing a word is off. A run of the middle-dot token
'··' (one degenerate document) gives its largest value.
"""
import re
import unicodedata

READS = ()

ONE_LETTER = re.compile(r"(\W*)([^\W\d_])")
# typical size of a space-led non-Latin single letter, by script
SPACED = {"GREEK": 1.5, "ARABIC": 1.5, "HEBREW": 1.4, "CYRILLIC": 0.9, "THAI": 0.5}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if tok == "··":
        return carry, 9.0
    m = ONE_LETTER.fullmatch(tok)
    if m is None:
        return carry, 0.0
    pre, letter = m.group(1), m.group(2)
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2] if len(prefix.token_strings) > 1 else ""
    continues_word = pre == "" and prev[-1:].isalpha()
    if continues_word:
        return carry, 0.0
    upper = letter.isupper()
    if letter.isascii():
        if pre == " ":
            return carry, 0.32 if upper else 0.15
        if pre == "":
            return carry, 0.27 if upper else 0.05
        return carry, 0.52 if upper else 0.21
    script = unicodedata.name(letter, "").split(" ")[0]
    if pre == " ":
        return carry, SPACED.get(script, 0.5)
    return carry, 0.1

    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]

    word = word + core.lower() if core[:1].isalpha() else ""

    for stem, v in STEM_VALUES.items():

Kana in the recent context turns on a signed lexical response.  Temporal
endpoints and identifying words in this lexicon are positive. Several kanji
roots are negative, but completing a familiar compound can weaken that response.

KANA = regex.compile(r'[\p{Script=Hiragana}\p{Script=Katakana}]')

    if word in {'最初', '最後'}:  # first, last
        return 5.1
    if word == '最近':  # recently
        return 2.8
    if word == '降' and before.endswith('以'):  # 以降: from ... onward
        return 3.5
    if word == '是非':  # certainly, by all means
        return 3.4
    if word in {'指定', '特定', '具体的'}:  # designated, specific, concrete
        return 3.8
    if word == '自身':  # oneself; 自分自身 is an emphatic self-reference
        return 1.0 if before.endswith('自分') else 2.1
    if word == '体' and before.endswith('自'):  # 自体: itself
        return 6.3
    if word == '側':  # side
        return 4.4
    if word == '際':  # occasion, boundary; 国際 means international
        return 1.0 if before.endswith('国') else 3.2
    if word == '反':  # reversal, opposition
        return 4.7
    if word == '等':  # etc., and the like
        return 2.5
    if word == '化':  # change, -ization; 強化 means strengthening
        return 0.8 if before.endswith('強') else 2.0
    if word == '社':  # company; 会社 and 神社 are weaker
        return -1.5 if before.endswith(('会', '神')) else -4.8
    if word == '現':  # current, appear; 実現 means realization

        return -1.3 if classification else -6.0

    return 0.0

    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]

"""A surface-grammar approximation for Japanese and Korean nominal phrases.

Japanese clause nominalizers and Korean 'thing/fact' forms are strongest.
Dependent nouns, counters and a few spatial/time markers have smaller
responses. Kanji rules require recent kana, to distinguish Japanese from
Chinese. Longer merged phrases do not inherit a constituent's response.
Most other tokens, including unmodeled verb stems, receive zero.
"""

import re
import regex

def expression_value(text, japanese, after_number):
    t = text.strip()
    # Japanese nominalized clauses, with topic, subject or question particles.
    if re.fullmatch(r'(する|る)?の[はも]', t):
        return 7.8
    if re.fullmatch(r'(する|る)のが', t):
        return 8.1
    if t == 'のが':
        return 5.7
    if t == 'のか':
        return 3.0
    if t == 'のです':
        return 3.5
    if t == 'んです':
        return 2.2
    if t == 'んだ':
        return 0.9
    if t == 'ん':
        return 1.9
    if t == 'っ':  # the small kana used for gemination
        return 2.6
    if t == 'わけ':  # reason / circumstance
        return 4.1
    if t == 'よう':  # manner / resemblance
        return 2.2
    m = re.fullmatch(r'(する|る|す)?こと([がはもにをで]?)', t)
    if m:
        return {'': 1.3, 'が': 3.0, 'は': 1.7, 'も': 1.4,
                'に': 0.25, 'を': 0.5, 'で': 0.45}[m[2]]
    if t in ('それ', 'それは', 'それが', 'これが', 'そんな'):
        return 1.5

    # Korean dependent 'thing' nouns and their contractions/case endings.
    if text in (' 거', ' 건'):
        return 8.8
    if text in (' 것', ' 것이', ' 것은'):
        return 5.8
    if text in (' 것으로', ' 것을', ' 걸', ' 게'):
        return 2.3
    if t in ('거', '건', '것', '걸', '게'):
        return 1.7
    if t in ('중', '후'):  # in the middle / after
        return (4.0 if t == '중' else 3.2) if text.startswith(' ') else 1.5
    if t == '점':  # point, aspect, fact
        return 6.3 if text.startswith(' ') else 2.0
    if t in ('등', '개', '장', '대', '순'):  # etc.; units; order
        return 2.0 if text.startswith(' ') else 0.8

    if japanese:
        if t == '中':  # inside / during
            return 2.1
        if t == '外':  # outside
            return -4.4
        if t == '後':  # after
            return 2.5
        if t == '件':  # counter for cases or matters
            return 7.0
        if t == '点':  # points/items, or an abstract aspect

    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]

    data = pending + raw

    number = bool(tail) and (tail[-1].isdigit() or tail[-1] in '十百千万億')

layers.1.mlp.down_proj:5998 is sparse. It sits near zero on almost every token and spikes on a
few kinds of word that head a noun phrase built from a clause or a dependent noun:

1. Japanese nominaliser の followed by a particle or copula, usually after a verb or adjective:
   のは, のが, のも, のです, のか, ことが, ことは ("doing X is ...", "the fact that ...").
   Strongest; e.g. 「...ことが」「...するのが」.
2. Korean dependent nouns, the "thing / one" words that follow a verb or adjective:
   것, 거, 걸, 건, 게, 개, 중, 후, 등, 장, 번, 겁, with a particle attached (것이, 것은 ...).
3. A few Japanese dependent or formal nouns: 後, 店, 理由, 一方. These are weaker.

The program predicts a fixed strength per class for a matching token and 0 elsewhere. It
reads only the current token. Context (e.g. whether the text is Japanese) was tested and did not
help. The class strengths are rounded means fitted on training rows.

KOREAN_PARTICLES = ("이", "은", "을", "를", "는", "가", "도", "만", "에", "으로")
JAPANESE_DEPENDENT_NOUNS = {"後", "店", "理由", "一方"}

NOMINALISER_STRENGTH = 4
KOREAN_STRENGTH = 3
DEPENDENT_STRENGTH = 1


def strength(token):
    """Strength of a single token string (its leading space ignored)."""
    word = token.lstrip(" ")
    if word.endswith(NOMINALISER_TOKENS):
        return NOMINALISER_STRENGTH
    if word in KOREAN_DEPENDENT_NOUNS or any(

    ):
        return KOREAN_STRENGTH
    if word in JAPANESE_DEPENDENT_NOUNS:

    return 0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """This position's predicted activation: the strength of the current token, if it is a class word."""
    return carry, float(strength(prefix.token_strings[-1]))

"""Predict an initial-context response from familiar token properties.

Activity is concentrated at the first token of each attention-reset document
(and persists if that same token is repeated). Estimate its size from word
frequency, grammatical class, script and whitespace. Away from this opening
run predict zero. Individual words have large differences this approximation
cannot capture.
"""
import regex
import wordnet
from wordfreq import zipf_frequency

READS = ()

ARTICLES = set('a an the'.split())
DEMONSTRATIVES = set('this that these those'.split())
NEGATION = set('no not never neither nothing nobody none'.split())
FUNCTION_WORDS = set('''
    i me my mine myself we us our ours ourselves you your yours yourself
    yourselves he him his himself she her hers herself it its itself
    they them their theirs themselves
    in on at to of from by for with without as into over under about
    between through after before during within against among
    and or but nor so if because although while when than whether
    be am is are was were been being have has had do does did
    can could may might will would shall should must
'''.split())


def opening_value(text):
    word = text.strip()
    if word.startswith('<|'):
        return 0.7
    if not word:
        return -0.6 + 1.9 * ('\t' in text)
    if word.isnumeric():
        return -0.4
    space = text.startswith(' ')
    if not word.isalpha():
        return (-0.95 + 1.3 * (len(word) > 1) + 1.4 * space
                + 1.8 * (not word.isascii()))
    if not regex.search(r'\p{Script=Latin}', word):
        if regex.search(r'[\p{Script=Hiragana}\p{Script=Katakana}]', word):
            return 3.4
        if regex.search(r'\p{Script=Cyrillic}', word):
            return 1.9
        if regex.search(r'\p{Script=Greek}', word):
            return 3.1
        return 2.3
    lower = word.lower()
    frequency = zipf_frequency(lower, 'en')
    value = 2.35 - 0.835 * max(0.0, frequency - 3.5) + 1.1 * space
    if 'adjective' in wordnet.parts_of_speech(lower):
        value -= 1.0
    if lower in ARTICLES:
        value -= 0.7
    if lower in DEMONSTRATIVES:
        value -= 2.1
    if lower in FUNCTION_WORDS:
        value -= 0.5
    if lower in NEGATION:
        value += 3.9
    return value


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    token = prefix.token_bytes[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        opening = True
    else:
        opening = carry[1] is not None and carry[1] == token
    if not opening:
        return (doc, None), 0.0
    return (doc, token), float(opening_value(prefix.token_strings[-1]))

"""Detect the second digit of a likely year: mainly 19 or 20, weakly 18.

Calendar language, dates, and citations strengthen the response. Quantities,
number notation, and code weaken it. Chinese 九 after 一 gets a fixed response;
all other tokens predict zero. Only preceding text is used, reset per document.
"""
import calendar
import re
import regex
READS = ()

MONTH = r'\b(?:' + '|'.join(
    list(calendar.month_name)[1:] + list(calendar.month_abbr)[1:]) + r')\b'
YEAR_CUE = (r'\b(?:in|since|during|until|before|after|between|from|'
            r'circa|year|years|the)\s+(?:the\s+)?$')
QUANTITY = (r'\b(?:about|approximately|roughly|nearly|exactly|than|'
            r'least|most|equals?)\s+$|(?:約|约)$')
MEASURE = (r'\b(?:velocity|radius|diameter|temperature|mass|length|height|'
           r'speed|distance|volume|count|integer|equation|prime)\b')
EXPLICIT_DATE = (r'\bborn\b|(?:\bdate\b|\bcopyright\b|©)[^\d]{0,40}$|'
                 r'\bet\s+al[.,\s(]*$|\b(?:early|late|mid)[ -]*$|'
                 r'\bFY\s*$|(?:于|在|至|到)$')


def has(pattern, text):
    return bool(re.search(pattern, text, re.I))


def year_score(before, historical):
    tail = before[-80:]
    end = before.rstrip()
    n = max(1, len(tail))

    # Prose versus dense numbers; an extra boost for Han-script prose.
    value = 0.892 + 0.246 * historical
    value += 0.772 * sum(c.isalpha() for c in tail) / n
    value -= 1.139 * sum(c.isdigit() for c in tail) / n
    value += 0.685 * len(regex.findall(r'\p{Script=Han}', tail)) / n

    # Calendar phrases and bibliographic context.
    value += 0.976 * has(YEAR_CUE, before)
    value += 0.625 * has(MONTH, before[-35:])
    value += 1.218 * has(EXPLICIT_DATE, before[-40:])
    value += 0.529 * end.endswith('(')
    value += 0.155 * min(3, len(re.findall(r'(?:19|20)\d\d', tail)))

    # Competing readings: quantities, decimal/time notation, and code.
    value -= 0.366 * end.endswith(('-', '–', '—', ':'))
    value -= 0.455 * (has(r'\d[.,:]\s*$', before) or
        end.endswith(('$', '£', '€', '¥', '=', '+', '*', '^')))
    value -= 0.768 * (has(QUANTITY, before) or has(MEASURE, before[-35:]) or
        has(r'(?<!\d)\d{1,3}\s+(?:to|and)\s+$', before))
    code_marks = min(8, sum(c in '{}[]=;_\\<>|' for c in tail)) / 8
    indented = has(r'(?:^|\n)(?: {3,}|\t)[^\n]*$', before)
    value -= 0.382 * (code_marks + indented)
    return max(0., min(3.7, value))


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    text = carry[1] if carry is not None and carry[0] == doc else ''
    s = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    value = 0.0
    if s in ('0', '8', '9'):
        run = re.search(r'[0-9]+$', text)
        digits = run[0] if run else ''
        if (digits, s) in (('1', '8'), ('1', '9'), ('2', '0')):
            value = year_score(text[:-1], s != '0')
            if s == '8':
                value *= 0.2
    elif s == '九' and text.endswith('一'):
        value = 3.5
    return (doc, (text + s)[-160:]), value

then "0") as the start of a standalone number, the century is settled and the
decade digits are next. The unit fires at that point, strongly for "19" and less
for "20", and less when the number is glued to a decimal, version or code

def step(carry, prefix, upstream):

    if word in ENGLISH_WORDS:
        carry["english"] += 1
    if any(is_cyrillic(char) for char in token):

    return carry, float(value)

"""Predict mostly negative responses to short r-p / r-f spelling fragments.

Pairs can be inside a token or straddle its left edge; p-f and vowel-separated
variants have weaker rules. Length, case, spacing and preceding vowels adjust
the strength. Transliteration applies these tests to other alphabets, not Han.
A small tail continues into the next short alphabetic fragment.

Separate rules cover URL separators, runs of middle dots, and a colon after
document-initial 'Title'. State resets at document boundaries. This captures
spelling and formatting patterns, not every fragment's context-specific gain.
"""
import re
import regex
from functools import lru_cache
from anyascii import anyascii

READS = ()


@lru_cache(maxsize=65536)
def spelling(text):
    if regex.search(r"\p{Script=Han}", text):
        return "", False
    roman = anyascii(text)
    return roman, roman != text


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    previous, prior = ("", 0.0)
    at_start = carry is None or carry[0] != doc
    title = False
    if not at_start:
        previous, prior, title = carry[1:]
    s, foreign = spelling(text)
    p, _ = spelling(previous)
    lo, prev = s.lower(), p.lower()
    value = -0.001
    strength = 0.0
    cross = prev.endswith("r") and lo.startswith(("p", "f"))
    pair = re.search(r"r[pf]|pf", lo) if len(lo.strip()) <= 5 else None
    # A new consonant pair crossing the token boundary.
    if cross and len(s) <= 4:
        value -= 5.639
        value += 1.975 * (len(prev.strip()) == 1)
        value += 1.269 * (len(s) - 1)
        value -= 1.172 * prev.endswith(("ir", "ur", "uer"))
        value += 1.149 * s.isupper()
        value -= 0.625 * lo.startswith("p")
        value += 1.257 * foreign
        value += 0.563 * min(len(prev.strip()) - 1, 4)
        value -= 0.711 * p.isupper()
        value += 0.37 * p.startswith(" ")
        strength = 1.0
    # Inside a short token, surrounding letters damp the response.
    elif pair:
        value += {"rp": -3.392, "rf": -3.243,
                  "pf": -1.091}[pair.group()]
        value += 0.773 * min(len(lo[:pair.start()].strip()), 6)
        value += 1.158 * min(len(lo[pair.end():]), 6)
        value += 0.734 * s.startswith(" ")
        value -= 0.26 * s.strip().isupper()
        value += 0.119 * (pair.group() == "rp" and
                          lo[pair.end():].startswith("h"))
        strength = 0.6
    elif prev.endswith("p") and lo.startswith("f"):
        value -= 0.581
    elif prev.endswith("r") and re.match("[aeiou][pf]", lo):
        value -= 0.397
    elif re.search("r[aeiou][pf]", lo):
        value -= 0.019
    if lo.isalpha() and not s.startswith(" ") and len(lo) <= 5:
        value -= 0.161 * prior
    if text.startswith("://"):
        value -= 1.248
    if (len(text) > 1 and set(text) == {"·"} and
            (at_start or set(previous) == {"·"})):
        value -= 1.905
    if text == ":" and title:
        value -= 3.68
    heading = at_start and text.strip() == "Title"
    return (doc, text, strength, heading), min(-0.001, value)

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:6014 -- a "p or f inside a split word" detector, plus URL schemes.

What the component does, in plain terms
  It is almost silent, except for negative dips on a few kinds of token:
  1. The "://" that follows "http" / "https" in a URL: about -1.3 on average.
  2. A short piece (1 to 3 letters) of a word that was already split into several tokens,
     when the piece contains the letter p or f. Examples: "pen" in Antwer|pen, "f" in
     Queer|f|ingern, "fc" in er|fc, "p" in pur|ples, "pn" in sier|pn|ia. Piece-level values
     are about -0.3 (lowercase) and -0.2 (capitalised), with large spikes on rare words.
  Everything else is about zero. A p or f piece that begins a word, or a long piece, is ignored.

What the program does
  It looks only at the newest token and the one before it, in the same document.
  The number it returns is the component's predicted activation at that position.
  The predictor explains only a few percent of the variance: the biggest dips are on
  unusual, rare word fragments, and nothing simple here predicts their size.
"""

READS = ()

URL_SCHEME_SEPARATOR = "://"
URL_VALUE = -1.2
LOWER_PIECE_VALUE = -0.3
UPPER_PIECE_VALUE = -0.2
MAX_PIECE_LETTERS = 3


def _is_letters(text):
    # letters only, with no leading space: a fragment of a word
    return text.isalpha()


def _continues_word(previous):
    # the previous token is letters too (with an optional leading space): the word is still going
    return _is_letters(previous) or (previous[:1] == " " and _is_letters(previous[1:]))


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tokens = prefix.token_strings
    token = tokens[-1]
    if token == URL_SCHEME_SEPARATOR:
        return None, URL_VALUE
    has_p_or_f = "p" in token.lower() or "f" in token.lower()
    if not (_is_letters(token) and len(token) <= MAX_PIECE_LETTERS and has_p_or_f):
        return None, 0.0
    same_document = len(tokens) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if not (same_document and _continues_word(tokens[-2])):
        return None, 0.0
    return None, UPPER_PIECE_VALUE if token[0].isupper() else LOWER_PIECE_VALUE

"""Recognize local n-a-consonant spelling fragments, also across token breaks:
for example, nap / nak / nach, or a token ending n followed by ac.
Transliteration applies the same rule to alphabetic scripts. Closed fragments
are stronger than continued or deeply embedded syllables; consonants, casing,
and script adjust their size. Greek vowels and a few n-word families also have
negative responses. State resets between documents. This approximates spelling
responses, not pronunciation or word meaning, and misses byte-fragment effects.
"""
import re
import regex
from functools import lru_cache
from anyascii import anyascii

READS = ()
# Following consonant: closed fragment, continued syllable, within-token correction.
COMPLETIONS = {
    'k': (6.28, 1.35, -0.60),
    'c': (4.74, 1.31, 0.00),
    'ch': (4.78, 2.78, -1.45),
    'ck': (2.56, 2.13, 0.00),
    'p': (5.16, 1.11, -0.57),
    'b': (4.29, 0.85, 0.00),
    'm': (3.46, 1.40, -0.80),
    'g': (2.86, 0.94, 0.00),
    'j': (1.91, 0.99, 0.00),
    'st': (3.00, 0.99, 0.00),
    's': (0.99, 0.69, 0.00),
    't': (0.96, 0.27, 0.00),
    'd': (1.67, 0.25, 0.00),
    'l': (0.76, 0.43, 0.00),
    'r': (1.32, 0.16, 0.00),
    'v': (1.88, 0.86, 0.00),
    'h': (1.77, 0.72, 0.00),
    'z': (1.21, 0.72, 0.00),
    'n': (-0.63, -0.42, 0.59),
    'zh': (3.39, 0.00, 0.00),
    'kh': (2.27, 0.22, 0.00),
    'sh': (0.65, 0.26, 0.00),
    'ts': (0.58, 1.00, 0.00),
    'other': (1.28, 0.02, 0.00),
}
DIGRAPHS = ('ch', 'ck', 'st', 'zh', 'kh', 'sh', 'ts')

@lru_cache(maxsize=32768)
def letters(text):
    if regex.search(r'[\p{Han}\p{Hiragana}\p{Katakana}\p{Hangul}]', text):
        return ''
    if text.endswith(('\\n', '\\r')):
        return ''
    return anyascii(text).lower()


def response(text, previous, older):
    cur, prev, old = letters(text), letters(previous), letters(older)
    word = cur.lstrip()
    short_n = prev.endswith('n') and len(prev.strip()) <= 4
    value = .00275
    if word in ('nation', 'nations'):
        value -= 2.51
    if word == 'nearest':
        value -= 3.16
    if word in ('nin', 'nine'):
        value -= .37
    if re.fullmatch(r'name(s|d)?', word):
        value -= .38

    direct, delayed, tail = False, False, None
    scale = 1.
    if short_n and cur.startswith('a'):
        tail = cur[1:]
    elif 'na' in word:
        direct = True
        i = word.rfind('na')
        tail = word[i+2:]
        scale = .8 if text[:1].isspace() else .7
        scale *= 1 if i == 0 else (.5 if i == 1 else .1)
    elif (prev.endswith('na') or (prev == 'a' and old.endswith('n'))
          ) and cur[:1].isalpha():
        delayed, tail, scale = True, cur, .6

    if tail is not None:
        match = re.match('[bcdfghjklmnpqrstvwxz]+', tail)
        cluster = match[0] if match else ''
        consonant = next((d for d in DIGRAPHS if cluster.startswith(d)),
                         cluster[:1])
        key = consonant if consonant in COMPLETIONS else 'other'
        rest = tail[len(cluster):]
        if len(cluster) > len(key):
            scale *= .65
        if rest:
            scale /= 1 + .2 * (len(rest)-1)
        closed, continued, correction = COMPLETIONS[key]
        strength = (continued if rest else closed) if cluster or not tail else 0.
        if direct:
            strength += -.22 + correction
            if text.lstrip()[:1].isupper():
                strength += .26
        if delayed:
            strength += .27
        if text[:1].isupper() and text[1:].islower():
            strength -= .39
        if regex.search(r'\p{Cyrillic}', text):
            strength += .06
        value += scale * strength
        if re.fullmatch(r'(pp|bb|mm|gg|kk|tt)(ed|ing|er|ers)', tail):
            value += (1 if not direct else .8) * 3.63
        if not tail:
            value -= .85 * scale
            initial = text.strip()[:1]
            if not direct and regex.match(r'\p{Latin}', initial) and initial not in 'aA':
                value += 1.22 * scale
        if regex.search(r'\p{Greek}', text):
            value += 3.36 * (scale if len(tail) < 2 else scale*.2)

    if short_n and cur and not cur[0].isspace():
        initial = cur[0]
        penalty = {'e': -.12, 'o': -.20, 'i': .05}.get(initial, 0.)
        if initial.isascii() and initial.isdigit():
            penalty = -.25
        if regex.search(r'\p{Greek}', text):
            penalty += {'e': -.41, 'o': -1.98, 'i': -.05, 'n': -.53}.get(initial, 0.)
        value += penalty / (1 + .4*(len(cur)-1))
    return value


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        previous, older = '', ''
    else:
        _, previous, older = carry
    current = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    return (doc, current, previous), float(response(current, previous, older))

"""Layer-1 MLP component 6015 (down_proj): a "na-syllable" detector.

What it responds to: a token that is a short word fragment beginning with the syllable
"na" (Latin) or "на" (Cyrillic) and followed directly by a consonant, with no vowel
after it: nap, nach, nak, nam, nag, нап, нач, нам, nas, над. These push the residual
stream positively. The response is strongest for stop, affricate or m/k-like
consonants (p, k, m, ch, g, б, г, ч, п) and when the fragment begins a word (it has a
leading space). Ordinary words that start with "na" followed by a vowel (name, nation,
nearest) do not fire; "nation(s)" and "nearest" are mildly negative.

Everything else is 0. The program looks only at the current token's text, so its
prediction is a fixed function of which token it is, and it uses no earlier context.
"""

import re

READS = ()

NA = r"(na|на)"
# Stop, affricate or nasal-like consonant right after "na": nap, nach, nak, nam, нап, нач.
STRONG = r"(ch|[pkmgbчмкбгп])"
# Any other one or two consonants (no vowel) after "na": nas, nad, nav, над.
WEAK = r"[bcdfghjklqrstvwxzбвгджзклмпрстфхцчшщй]{1,2}"


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    raw = prefix.token_strings[-1]  # this token, decoded alone
    word = raw.strip().lower()
    starts_word = raw.startswith(" ")  # a leading space: the fragment begins a word
    if re.fullmatch(NA + STRONG, word):
        return None, 4.0 if starts_word else 2.0
    if re.fullmatch(NA + WEAK, word):
        return None, 1.0 if starts_word else 0.3
    if word in ("nation", "nations", "nearest"):
        return None, -2.5
    return None, 0.0
